audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Veigar/Veigar while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Ekko on all seven rows. The full layer also grades the lane TRICKY 7/10 while every content sentence calls it lopsided in Ekko's favour.
audit.why: Veigar has no dash and no blink; his only lockdown is Event Horizon at 20s rank 1 falling to 14s. Ekko's E is 9s. That means roughly half the lane has no answer to a dive at all, which is why the chart, the content prose and a 53.59% win rate over 1183 games all agree.
audit.corrected: Full phases[0..6].side -> Ekko with ratings raised, whys rewritten in the same group; diff -> FAVOURED, diffRating -> 4/10, tone -> green, and the two difficulty prose lines brought in line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike prose carried no cooldowns even though packet counted five sequencing cues.
audit.why: Event Horizon 20/18.5/17/15.5/14 is the entire punish window and was never numbered; Primordial Burst is 120s at rank 1, Baleful Strike 6s falling to 4s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2].why, phases[3].why and dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated the two interactions that decide this lane: Primordial Burst scales on the target's MISSING health, and Phenomenal Evil is permanent AP gained from every spell that hits a champion.
audit.why: Riot's text: R 'increasing based on the target's missing health' and P 'Striking an enemy Champion with a spell or scoring a takedown grants Veigar permanently increased Ability Power.' Together they mean chip damage is never free against him and half HP is exactly the threshold where his ultimate becomes lethal. Neither was on the page.
audit.corrected: Stated in enemyWin, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.feeding and ahead.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Event Horizon 20s->14s, Baleful Strike 6s->4s, Primordial Burst 120s.

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: your E dash and Q slow beat a kit with only skillshots at point-blank range.

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: Still yours: Baleful Strike needs hits to stack, and E on a 9s cooldown makes every one dodgeable.

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 — the longest punish window in the lane. Step in whenever it is down.

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Keep abusing it: he has no dash at all, so a whiffed cage buys you a free string and a plate.

edits.before: Chronobreak online — your aggression gets a save file. Trade like the rewind exists, because it does.
edits.after: Chronobreak online: 110s of insurance against the one cage that could ever actually catch you out.

edits.before: First item spike: the full string deletes half bars and the rewind erases the counter-argument.
edits.after: First item: the string runs down an escape-less Veigar before Primordial Burst comes back up.

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive the carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Late you pick and survive: W-stun him where he stands, dive, and Chronobreak out of the cage entirely.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Check it before every step-up. - R Chronobreak is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and 14s maxed — the longest cooldown in his kit and your whole window. Only the cage EDGE stuns: hold near the centre or leave before it forms, and never dash into the wall. - Baleful Strike is 6s falling to 4s. - Primordial Burst is 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 — that is a long stretch in which a mage with no dash has nothing at all to stop your E.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Primordial Burst scales off your MISSING health, so half HP is when it kills — not the moment to be without R.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the cage EDGE, stacking Phenomenal Evil off every hit, and executing your missing health.

edits.before: If Veigar takes first blood, tighten up: Event Horizon (Cage) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q passes and stay relevant through W stuns and R picks.
edits.after: If Veigar takes first blood, remember every spell he lands is permanent AP — deny the stacks and never trade into a loaded cage. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q from 1075.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry by running him down the moment his cage is spent — one carry per rewind cycle; R is the weapon, not an apology.

edits.before: Ahead, compound the tempo: string Veigar off every contact, dive the rivers insured, and rewind the audits — fed Ekko makes time a one-way argument.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the stacks: string Veigar off every contact, deny him Baleful Strike execute gold, and dive insured — he has no dash to leave on.

notes: Full chart was stale on all seven rows AND the difficulty grade contradicted its own content layer: full said TRICKY 7/10 while every content sentence and a 53.59% win rate describe a lane Ekko controls from minute one. I moved the full layer onto the content/packet values. Content win[] already read Ekko on all seven rows, so no paired win[N] edit exists to propose (before would equal after); the seven side edits plus ratings and whys are the atomic group. Left carryRating at 7.5/10 — Veigar's late-game threat is real even when the lane is not. suspectNames flagged 'Baleful Strikes' in wants.you[0]; it is a trivial pluralisation of the correct name and sits in a content field I had no other reason to touch, so I left it rather than spend an edit — flagging it here instead. Dark Matter's kit cooldown reads 0 because Phenomenal Evil stacks reduce it; I asserted no number for it.
